subject: Pricing annex — ramp smoothing & fee cushion: redline questions
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@orionhealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Price <j.price@orionhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines on pricing annex — ramp smoothing & fee cushion

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the latest pricing annex. Our finance team reviewed the 'ramp smoothing' and 'fee cushion' language and left several redlines in the attached PDF (ORION_Redline_Orderform_v2.pdf). Two items we want to be explicit about before legal signs off:

1) True-up treatment during the first 90 days of ramp — the redline adds a carveout that would delay any penalty until month 4. Can you confirm Redwood's operational tolerance for that delay?

2) Fee cushion calculation — we flagged that the formula references 'monthly billable tokens' but doesn't define rounding or treatment of fractional months for newly onboarded SKUs. We need deterministic behavior for invoicing.

We attached a spreadsheet with a worked example (Orion_Pricing_Annex_v3.xlsx). If you could loop in ops/finance suggestions and provide a short note of how Redwood would implement (and an alternate minimal legal wording), we can forward to our GC.

Thanks — I appreciate a quick turnaround on this.

Best,
Maria Torres
Head of Cloud Procurement
Orion Health Systems

Attachments: ORION_Redline_Orderform_v2.pdf (PDF redline summary), Orion_Pricing_Annex_v3.xlsx (worked examples)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@orionhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines on pricing annex — ramp smoothing & fee cushion

Maria — thanks for the clear note and the worked example. Quick reply to scope expectations:

- Operational tolerance: Redwood can accept a 90-day grace window for penalty enforcement on ramp (i.e., no retroactive penalties for months 1–3) provided that the ramp is explicitly defined in the onboarding worksheet and that Orion commits to the forecast cadence. We need clear cutover dates to avoid ambiguous billing.

- Fee cushion rounding: we propose (a) compute on a per-SKU basis monthly, (b) round up to the nearest whole unit for invoicing, and (c) carry fractional remainder into the subsequent month rather than truncating. That yields predictable invoices and aligns with our existing billing pipeline.

I've asked Ben (pricing ops) to draft minimal legal language and Laura to confirm the invoicing behavior from our billing engine. We'll circulate a suggested redline by EOD tomorrow.

— Karthik
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Suggested legal wording for ramp/cushion (draft)

Karthik / Laura — draft language below that I think addresses Orion's asks while preserving our billing controls. Paste this into the redline PDF if useful.

--- DRAFT Wording ---
Ramp smoothing: For the purposes of invoicing and any applicable true-up, (i) no penalties shall be assessed for the first ninety (90) days following initial commercial launch of a given SKU (the "Ramp Period"), provided Customer delivers a forecast in accordance with the Onboarding Worksheet, and (ii) any shortfall attributable to the Ramp Period shall be captured in the subsequent true-up period and billed in the next invoice cycle.

Fee cushion computation: Unit fees shall be calculated per SKU on a monthly basis. Where a calculation results in a fractional unit, Redwood shall round up to the next whole unit for invoice presentation, and any fractional remainder shall be carried forward and aggregated in the following month's calculation.

--- end draft ---

Laura: confirm that our billing engine supports 'round up and carry forward' as written (I think it's OK; flags if not). If this is green, we'll send to Maria with a brief implementation note.

-Ben
Senior Pricing Analyst
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@orionhealth.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Price <j.price@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines on pricing annex — ramp smoothing & fee cushion

Karthik / Ben — thanks, that draft is clear and maps to our expectations. Two follow-ups before we send to GC:

- Can Redwood add a one-line example into the annex (not the legal body) that shows the 'round up and carry forward' with numbers similar to our spreadsheet? That makes internal approvals faster.

- For the Ramp Period language: can you confirm whether the 'subsequent true-up period' could push billable adjustments beyond quarter boundary? Our procurement policy prefers adjustments within the first billing quarter; if your approach can guarantee aggregation and billing no later than the immediately following invoice cycle after the true-up calculation, we can sign off.

If you can confirm both items in writing, we'll move it to our GC.

Best,
Maria

Attachments: none

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@orionhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redlines on pricing annex — ramp smoothing & fee cushion

Maria — quick confirmation:

1) We'll add a one-line worked example table into the annex (non-operational/legal section) mirroring your spreadsheet values — I'll attach a PDF extract for review.

2) Billing cadence: true-up aggregation will be reflected on the first invoice following the true-up calculation. Practically, that means adjustments will appear on the invoice cycle immediately following the true-up and will not be intentionally deferred beyond that cycle. That satisfies the "within the billing quarter" ask so long as Orion's true-up timetable aligns to a quarter boundary; if your true-up dates fall mid-quarter, the adjustment will appear on the next invoice (which may cross quarter boundaries).

We'll push the redline and the annex example to you by EOD tomorrow and include a short implementation note for Orion finance. Thanks for moving quickly on this — we want to avoid back-and-forth with GC.

— Karthik
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Orc_Annex_WorkedExample_extract.pdf (stub)
